title: Signed Excess-Risk Recovery for Many Providers under Indirect Standardization
banked_reason: D0.5.G: delivered signed-support beta-min boundary instead of the weighted-MSE frontier; incremental below field and math-panel revise findings unrepaired; soundness not established.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is an order-sharp beta-min boundary for exact signed-support recovery, not the advertised weighted-MSE frontier of order (s/k) min{1, k log(ek/s)/n + delta^2 epsilon^2}; the MSE estimator, its sparsity-dependent rate, and its converse are entirely absent.

[D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.8 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

The estimator-side normalized pilot rate is assumed without primitive learner/training/sample-size conditions establishing that k max_a ||pi_a-q_a||_2 <= delta is achievable in this no-conditional-positivity regime; derive it from a specified pilot procedure or explicitly rescope the result as conditional on an oracle-supplied certified pilot.

The outcome-pilot L2 radius is likewise an un-discharged estimator-side condition: no primitive training conditions or achievability argument delivers ||m-h||_2 <= epsilon for the supplied h; discharge it or make the conditional/oracle scope explicit.

Exact sparsity is inert for the asserted sign frontier: the coordinatewise upper proof never uses it, and both lower bounds remain valid over the larger unrestricted class because their witnesses have support two (the nuisance witness may simply use one positive-negative pair). Remove it from the headline class or state a result that genuinely consumes s.

The headline frontier is evaluable and a genuine Stat contribution if its proof checks, but its positioning fails the cited-work coverage requirement: DaignaultSaarela2017, VarewyckEtAl2014, and ZengEtAl2024 appear in the bibliography/comparator material without a substantive relevance-and-difference sentence, and the closest fixed-provider indirect-standardization and high-dimensional-discrete-covariate result classes are not compared theorem-by-theorem to this signed-support, marginal-balance, empty-cell frontier.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 developed a clipped score and a beta-min boundary for exact signed-support recovery, with a refined partition-rich lower-bound class. D0.5 found that this changed the requested weighted-MSE target and graded the note incremental below the field floor. Math-panel setup findings remain unrepaired, so the archived note is not soundness-cleared; no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: For growing provider collections, an explicit clipped residual-covariance selector achieves simultaneous signed recovery above \(\rho_\star=\min\{1,\delta\epsilon+\sqrt{k\log(2k)/n}+k\log(2k)/n\}\) on every measurable covariate space, even with conditional propensity zeros and empty evaluation cells. An exact-pilot paired-provider family gives the sampling converse without covariate richness. The product-error converse needs only unbounded finite measurable partition complexity: for each mixture resolution \(M\), one may choose a resolution-specific equal-mass law \(\nu_M\). This enlarged class includes countably infinite discrete measurable spaces; on it the same scale is the matched minimax boundary. The target is the sign of indirect excess risk, not ratio mean squared error.
gap: Susmann et al. identify indirect provider excesses and derive fixed-provider efficient influence functions, while Kramer, Kennedy, and Opper study high-dimensional estimation risk and explicitly leave valid inference and testing open. Neither result gives an exact signed-support boundary when provider counts can be zero and pilot bias is only controlled through normalized \(L_2\) radii.
fill: The project supplies an all-sample thresholding rule and an order-matching converse at the scale \(\delta\epsilon+\sqrt{k\log k/n}+k\log k/n\), with clipping that remains defined for empty providers and lower families that use common pilots and exact marginal balance.
